question: MathOverflow 516372: do 2x2 plaquette energies on {0,1}^{Z^2} always have a periodic ground state?
convention: Tile index t = a + 2b + 4c + 8d for the 2x2 window [[a,b],[c,d]] = [[top-left, top-right],[bottom-left, bottom-right]]. Arrays are [row][col], row index increasing downward. Energy per site = average of J[t] over all 2x2 windows. Period lattice generated (in (row,col)) by (p,0) and (s,q): x[r+p][c] = x[r][c] and x[r+s][c+q] = x[r][c]. fundamental_domain is the p x q block rows 0..p-1, cols 0..q-1; patch64 is the 64x64 tiling starting at the origin. J entries equal to 10.0 mark 'forbidden' tiles (large penalty).
certification: certified_ground_state=true means energy_per_site equals (to 1e-7) an LP lower bound valid for every shift-invariant measure, so the periodic configuration is a true ground state.

examples.lower_bound_method: LP on 4x4 windows, forbidden tiles (J=10) as hard constraints
examples.label: diagonal staircase (shear 13/21)
examples.note: Found by random sweep as the largest LP(3x3) gap; strip optimum keeps changing up to p=16; exact optimum has vertical period 21 with shear 13 (Fibonacci numbers). Only certified with 4x4-window LP. Note: certification is for the SFT with the 6 J=10 tiles forbidden.

examples.label: diagonal staircase (shear 13/21)
examples.note: Gaussian J (all 16 tiles allowed). Strip optimum up to p=10 has period 4 (area 8) with LP(3x3) gap 6.7e-3; exact optimum is the period-21, shear-13 staircase, certified by LP on 4x4 windows.
